top.title: ‘No more playstation’ – Anthony Joshua welcomes baby girl
top.description: Nigerian-British boxing champion, Anthony Joshua, has announced the birth of his second child, a girl, noting that there is no more time for PlayStation or FIFA for him. Joshua and his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026. The pair also have an 11-year-old son, Joseph. The former two-time unified heavyweight champion revealed this in an interview with The Sun , which gained attention on Thursday, said having a daughter would help him better understand women and how to support them. “Now I’ve got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive. My daughter will give me firsthand experience of a woman’s power,” he said. Joshua disclosed that the family had yet to settle on a name for the newborn, but described her as his princess. “I’ve spoken to all the women in my family, and it’s amazing the amount of support that women give each other. We haven’t given her a name yet, but she’s my Princess,” he added. The 36 year old boxer described the birth as a huge blessing, revealing that he deliberately avoided finding out the baby’s sex during the pregnancy. “It’s been amazing, a big blessing and I can’t believe I’m a girl dad. I didn’t want to find the sex out during the pregnancy,” Joshua said. He also joked about how having a daughter could change some of the activities he shares with his son. “I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, ‘No more Fifa, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!’” he said. “I’m going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her, you know?” he said. He also spoke about the responsibilities of caring for a newborn, saying he was prepared to change nappies and go through the demands of raising a baby again. “I will change nappies, I’ve gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!” he added. The development comes as Joshua prepares for a reported December 11 showdown with fellow British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury. top.title: Cyberattack on service provider exposes payee data at 40 Irish credit unions
top.description: An attack on software provider Wellington IT exposed saved payee details held by around 40 Irish credit unions, prompting a minister to criticize the company's delay in notifying them. Robert Troy, Ireland's minister of state with responsibility for credit unions, said the breach happened in October but many affected institutions only learned of it in recent days. Troy told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that the breach occurred "sometime in October," and Wellington IT's delay in providing details to its credit union customers was "not acceptable." News of the issues affecting Irish credit unions broke on Tuesday, although the government said at the time it was only investigating a "possible cybersecurity incident" in the first instance, and did not name Wellington IT until Wednesday. Affected credit unions said attackers exploited a vulnerability in their provider's online banking platform between October 2 and 4. The flaw was closed on October 6. Troy said the affected credit unions were only informed for the first time in recent days. The exposed records concern payees saved in members' online banking accounts. Those records can also be linked to the members who created them. The information exposed varies between institutions and individual records, but disclosures list the following data types: Names on payee bank accounts and saved nicknames Business Identifier Codes (BICs) International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs) Sort codes Payment references Internal reference numbers that do not identify customers Payee addresses Credit unions including St. Canice's said online banking passwords, PINs, and login credentials were unaffected, and that the exposed payee details did not provide access to members' accounts or funds. St. Canice's warned members not to transfer money in response to anyone claiming it needed to be moved to safety because of the breach. The CEO of Belfast-based Wellington IT, Colin Mitchell, said in a statement that the company notified the affected organizations "as soon as we confirmed the potential risk to customer data." He said Wellington IT has engaged outside cybersecurity experts to help investigate the breach, and reported the matter to the relevant authorities. Mitchell added: "We are directly supporting our customers in their assessment of the potential impact on affected individuals and to help them meet any applicable regulatory obligations. "We recognize the importance of this matter to our customers and their members and are treating it with the utmost seriousness. We remain focused on completing a thorough investigation and communicating directly with our customers as the investigation progresses." top.title: Mera denies defection rumour to APC in Kebbi
top.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The African Democratic Congress (ADC) senatorial candidate for Kebbi North, Alhaji Ibrahim Muhammad Mera, has dismissed reports circulating on social media that he has defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State. Mera, in a statement signed by his Director-General, Media, Garba Muhammad Yeldu, on Thursday, said he had neither met nor held discussions with any APC official or member over a possible defection. He described the reports as fabricated, alleging that they were being circulated by individuals seeking to create confusion and distract him from pursuing his senatorial ambition under the ADC. Mera acknowledged that political parties were experiencing internal challenges but insisted that the crisis within the ADC would not make him abandon the party. He said the APC also had its internal disagreements, adding that he remained focused on his political ambition and the pursuit of the Kebbi North senatorial seat. The ADC candidate urged his supporters and constituents to disregard the reports, describing them as products of the rumour peddlers’ imagination. He also appealed to them to remain calm, peaceful and law-abiding while continuing to support the ADC. “I have never for once thought or made attempts to leave ADC. I remain focused and unrelenting in the pursuit of my mandate in my party,” he said. Mera warned those behind the reports to desist from spreading what he described as false information and assured his supporters of his continued loyalty to the ADC. nigeria.title: Leicester split with sponsor after row over porn actor partnership
nigeria.description: Leicester City have parted ways with front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game following a fan backlash over the gambling firm’s appointment of a porn actor as an ambassador. The crypto gaming company, which became a sponsor for the former Premier League champions in 2024, named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month. Fan group the Foxes Trust stated on November 4, stating their dismay over the partnership. “Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people’s lives, in particular young people,” it said. “Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?” Leicester, who now play in the third tier of English football, issued a statement on Wednesday saying the club and BC Game had “reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect”. “The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward,” it said. The club thanked BC Game for the “constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement”. The statement did not refer to the supporters’ stated objections. Leicester shocked the sporting world when they won the Premier League in 2016, following up with an FA Cup triumph five years later. But the club has fallen on hard times in recent years and are currently 11th in League One. nigeria.title: ‘Enjoy the ride’- Pierce Brosnan tells Pattinson, new James Bond 007
nigeria.description: Irish actor Pierce Brosnan, who once played the role of the world’s most famous spy, has welcomed Robert Pattinson to the “world of Bond”, urging him to “enjoy the ride”. “You are going to be magnificent,” Brosnan wrote in a post on Instagram, under a black-and-white picture of Pattinson dressed as secret agent James Bond in a tuxedo and brandishing a hand-gun. “It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength,” he added. Brosnan played Bond in four films from 1995 to 2002, including “GoldenEye” and “Tomorrow Never Dies”, before handing over to Daniel Craig. After months of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios on Monday named British actor Pattinson as the seventh performer to step into the coveted 007 role, replacing Craig. Pattinson became a global pop culture phenomenon with his vampire role in the “Twilight” saga before being cast as Batman. He also starred alongside Brosnan in the 2010 romantic drama “Remember Me”. Brosnan signed off his message with “Gra Mor, Pierce” — Irish for “big love”. Another Bond alum, George Lazenby, who played the agent in the 1969 film “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service”, said on social media: “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world.” Craig, who played Bond in five films from 2006 to 2021, has yet to react to Pattinson stepping into his shoes. nigeria.title: Police rescue 15 kidnapped victims in Kogi forest after gun battle
nigeria.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 kidnapped victims from a kidnappers’ den in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, following a fierce gun battle between security operatives and the abductors. The victims, comprising men, women and children, were rescued in the early hours of Wednesday, November 18, during an intelligence-led joint security operation involving the police, military, forest guards and local security outfits. The Commissioner of Police, Kogi State Command, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, disclosed this on Thursday while briefing journalists at the Police Headquarters in Lokoja. Bello Kankarofi said the operation was conducted on his directive, adding that the joint security team stormed the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. According to him, the superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some of them sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries. He said, “During the operation, the joint team advanced into the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. The superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.” The rescued victims were identified as Okuma Terlum, 47; Ojo Deborah, 23; Samuel Danjuma, three; Faith Raphael, 21; Emmanuella Raphael, three; Donald Tor, 31; Joseph Jonathan, 20; Tergu Joseph, 15; Samuel Joseph, eight; Engr. Joseph Adebija, 58; Lois Abiodun, 50; Chuks Obiakor, 45; Ola Olufemi, 58; Ankpe Godwin, 23; and Kuhwa Solomon, 25. The police commissioner also disclosed that two other female victims, identified simply as Joy and Nwakan, escaped from their abductors during the initial encounter in which the victims were taken captive. He further revealed that the security team came under another ambush by members of the criminal gang while conveying the rescued victims out of the forest. However, he said the operatives successfully repelled the attack and brought all 15 victims out safely. The victims, who reportedly endured considerable physical and psychological distress during their captivity, were subsequently debriefed and taken to St. John’s Catholic Hospital, Kabba, for medical attention. Although no arrests had been made as of the time of the briefing, the commissioner said actionable intelligence had been generated, while investigations were ongoing to track down the fleeing kidnappers and identify their sponsors. He commended the participating security agencies and local security outfits for their courage, resilience and collaboration, assuring residents of the command’s commitment to sustaining coordinated operations against kidnapping and other violent crimes. nigeria.title: 2027: SDP’s Adamu promises free education, electricity relief for small businesses in Nasarawa
nigeria.description: The Nasarawa State governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, has promised to introduce free education in public primary and secondary schools and remove electricity bills for small-scale businesses if elected in 2027. Adamu said the proposed interventions were aimed at reducing the financial pressure on ordinary families and business owners struggling to meet basic expenses. He made the promises on Wednesday, November 18, while addressing supporters and residents of Gade community in Karu Local Government Area of the state. The former police chief said his administration would ensure that parents no longer had to struggle to pay school fees for their children. “We do not see any reason why a family, whether it is a boy or a girl, should have children in primary or secondary school and still struggle to pay school fees,” he said. “Government is supposed to take responsibility for that. Therefore, our administration will end the suffering associated with paying school fees by providing free education across primary and secondary schools.” He also pledged to remove electricity bills for small-scale business operators, arguing that the cost of power had become an additional burden for people trying to earn a living. “Insha Allah, our administration will remove the burden of electricity bills on small-scale businesses,” he said. On security, Adamu promised to deploy his experience as a former police chief to address insecurity in the state, particularly the challenges confronting farmers. He said the situation had prevented many residents from accessing their farmlands and earning a livelihood. “We are also aware that insecurity has become a major challenge. Many people can no longer go to their farms because of insecurity. If elected, we will deploy our experience to ensure that citizens enjoy the security they deserve,” he said. Adamu also criticised the administration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state, asking residents to assess its performance before deciding whether to support it for another term. He warned that re-electing the ruling party would mean another eight years of hardship for residents. The SDP candidate said his decision to seek the governorship was driven by the need to improve the living conditions of ordinary people. He further asked Gade residents to nominate three representatives for his campaign council, saying they would serve as a link between the community and his team and monitor the fulfilment of promises made to them. nigeria.title: INEC backs code for independent tabulation of 2027 election results
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has endorsed a voluntary Code of Conduct for independent tabulation and publication of election results ahead of 2027. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the backing at a stakeholders’ roundtable convened by Yiaga Africa in Abuja. The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, states this in a statement he signed on Thursday in Abuja. According to Itodo, Amupitan, who was represented by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, said the code would strengthen transparency and public confidence. He warned that independently aggregated figures, projections and partial tallies must never be presented as official election results. “Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres of statutory authority,” the INEC boss stated. Amupitan outlined six guiding principles for the framework, including methodological integrity, accuracy, information integrity, data security, error accountability and voluntary compliance. Itodo said independent tabulation helps citizens to scrutinise election outcomes and assess credibility. The Yiaga Africa boss noted that differing methodologies and publication standards could cause confusion during sensitive collation periods if left uncoordinated. He stressed that a common code would establish minimum standards, curb premature declarations and ensure findings are backed by reliable verification. Itodo said Yiaga Africa was expected to lead further engagements to translate the agreed principles into a practical framework before the 2027 general elections. Participants at the forum included civil society groups, political parties, election observers, the National Broadcasting Commission and the Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria. Also in attendance were representatives of the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) and the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ). Stakeholders examined different tabulation models, including Yiaga Africa’s Processing Results Voter Tabulation (PRVT) and Election Results Analysis Dashboard (ERAD), alongside INEC’s Result Viewing Portal (IReV) aggregations. They agreed that organisations must clearly disclose their methodologies, data sources and margins of error to prevent public misinterpretation. A technical session also highlighted the need for human verification, audit trails, data security and transparent error-correction procedures. Media stakeholders emphasised the duty of journalists to verify figures and clearly distinguish independent tallies from official results declared by INEC. nigeria.title: Prince Harry says would rejoin military to fight Russia if needed
nigeria.description: Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday. “I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the western city of Lviv over the weekend. “If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.” Harry, a former British army officer and the younger son of King Charles III, made his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion to meet wounded veterans and medics. The prince is also the founder of the Invictus Games for wounded veterans and met athletes hoping to represent Ukraine at next year’s games in the British city of Birmingham. “Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, that doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he told the British daily’s “Ukraine: The Latest” podcast. “I feel very confident that Europe has a united front, and it would be fantastic to have more American support for that as well,” he added. Earlier on his weekend visit to Lviv he told wounded veterans and medics specialising in war injuries: “You’re going to win the war”. He repeated that sentiment on the podcast, insisting that “Ukraine are winning” and “there is no version where Russia is making any more advances”. The 42-year-old prince has previously spoken about being moved by witnessing death and life-changing injuries while on deployment in Afghanistan, and launched the Invictus Games in 2014 when he was still in the British army. Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the UK earlier this year from California amid an enduring rift with the royal family and his brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William. But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online. Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images. nigeria.title: I disobeyed my father’s order to delete succession video – Jimmy Odukoya
nigeria.description: The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has admitted disobeying his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, by retaining a succession video he was instructed to delete after the founder’s successful surgery in 2021. Odukoya described his decision to keep the recording as a grave mistake while addressing about 300 church workers on Wednesday, against the backdrop of the ongoing leadership crisis at the church. He explained that his father requested the recording before travelling to the United States for surgery because he feared he might not survive the procedure. According to Church Times, which reported details of the meeting, Odukoya said he personally recorded the message in which Taiwo identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor. However, following his successful operation, the late founder reportedly asked him to erase the recording, saying the circumstances that prompted its creation no longer applied. Rather than comply, Jimmy kept the video, a decision he now acknowledges was wrong. He also claimed that only a few people, including his sisters, knew about the recording, alleging that they were responsible for making it public. The video has become central to the leadership dispute at the church, with a faction of its Board of Trustees relying on its contents to withdraw recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor. The faction announced on November 17 that it had appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, citing Taiwo’s instruction that Areogun should succeed him. In the recording, the late founder said Areogun should take over if he died or became unable to communicate, while assigning Jimmy the roles of Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the youth church. Jimmy, however, has rejected the board faction’s decision, insisting that he remains the church’s legitimate Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. He told the workers that the disagreement with the board began about a year after he assumed office, when members allegedly asked him to relinquish his position as board chairman and concentrate on pastoral responsibilities. He also alleged that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, approached him to step aside to allow her to become board chairman. The disagreement was reportedly taken to the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, after Bishop Mike Okonkwo intervened. Jimmy further denied allegations that he misappropriated N250m donated to the church for a project, maintaining that the money remained intact and that economic challenges had delayed the project. He said he had restricted access to church funds and dismissed claims of financial misconduct. Although he maintained that he remained Senior Pastor, Jimmy expressed uncertainty about the conduct of the next Sunday service and said an advertised church programme would not hold to prevent further escalation of the dispute. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? entertainment.description: From left: Nigerian artists Asake, Seyi Vibez, and Burna Boy, whose songs appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. How else could Grand Theft Auto VI begin than with Nigerian artists featured in the music lineup of the biggest video game release of the year? As players around the world finally step into Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated open-world action-adventure title, Burna Boy , Asake , and Seyi Vibez are making sure Nigerian music is front and centre on the virtual streets of Vice City and the wider state of Leonida. Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) officially arrives today, Thursday, 19 November 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V first hit consoles. Developed and published by Rockstar Games, the open-world action-adventure game follows dual protagonists Jason and Lucia across the sun-soaked, neon-lit state of Leonida—a fictional take on Florida that brings players back to Vice City in the franchise’s largest map yet. Music has always been at the heart of the Grand Theft Auto universe, where players tune into curated in-game radio stations while driving or walking around town, and this sixth instalment takes African soundscapes seriously. At the centre of the Nigerian presence is AfroBank FM, a dedicated African music radio station inside Grand Theft Auto VI that is co-hosted by Grammy winner Burna Boy—credited on-air simply as Burna—alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax , who goes by Palmsy. Curated to spotlight everything from 20th-century African classics to contemporary Afrobeats, amapiano, and 3-step, the station features Asake’s 2022 hit “ Joha ” from his debut album Mr Money With The Vibe , as well as “ Giza “, the 2023 collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez from Burna Boy’s seventh studio album I Told Them …. Alongside those tracks, Burna Boy also appears on the game’s official companion soundtrack album, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, with his original song “ Bigger ” sitting on a 34-track roster that includes Travis Scott , Cardi B , Dua Lipa , SZA , Tame Impala , and Lana Del Rey . The African representation on AfroBank FM stretches beyond Nigeria too, sharing airwaves with Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor on “ Gye Wani ” and South African stars DJ Lag , Robot Boii , and Kamo Mphela on “ Shay’sana “. With players able to listen to Leonida’s terrestrial radio stations both in vehicles and on foot through in-game headphones, millions of gamers worldwide are now cruising through Vice City with Burna Boy on the mic and Asake and Seyi Vibez on heavy rotation. Decades later, he returned to the warm springs town with family, friends and business partners, “not to take away, but to help build something enduring in Ekiti.” Speaking as Chairman and Chief Launcher of Ikogosi Day 2026, Thanksgiving and Launch of the Oba’s Palace Project, on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the Chancellor of Ekiti State University set out a vision for Ikogosi built on intentional tourism, enterprise and heritage. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. To build that service culture, he called for a deeper, structured partnership between the Ikogosi Resort and the Hospitality Management Technology Department of the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti, which has already produced two sets of National Diploma graduates. The goal is for students to train alongside seasoned professionals while serving real guests. He also proposed alliances with leading international hospitality institutes to benchmark local teaching and service, noting that world-class hospitality must become Ekiti’s signature. He argued that the same commercial discipline must apply to the resources beneath the ground. “It is not enough to say we have clay or kaolin. We must ask: What are their exact industrial specifications? What can we competitively manufacture? And who is ready to buy?” he said. He tasked the Department of Geology at Ekiti State University, headed by Professor Yinka Aturamu , with establishing precise data on local deposits and mapping out what it would take to turn them into viable commercial enterprises. technology.description: An attack on software provider Wellington IT exposed saved payee details held by around 40 Irish credit unions, prompting a minister to criticize the company's delay in notifying them. Robert Troy, Ireland's minister of state with responsibility for credit unions, said the breach happened in October but many affected institutions only learned of it in recent days. Troy told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that the breach occurred "sometime in October," and Wellington IT's delay in providing details to its credit union customers was "not acceptable." News of the issues affecting Irish credit unions broke on Tuesday, although the government said at the time it was only investigating a "possible cybersecurity incident" in the first instance, and did not name Wellington IT until Wednesday. Affected credit unions said attackers exploited a vulnerability in their provider's online banking platform between October 2 and 4. The flaw was closed on October 6. Troy said the affected credit unions were only informed for the first time in recent days. The exposed records concern payees saved in members' online banking accounts. Those records can also be linked to the members who created them. The information exposed varies between institutions and individual records, but disclosures list the following data types: Names on payee bank accounts and saved nicknames Business Identifier Codes (BICs) International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs) Sort codes Payment references Internal reference numbers that do not identify customers Payee addresses Credit unions including St. Canice's said online banking passwords, PINs, and login credentials were unaffected, and that the exposed payee details did not provide access to members' accounts or funds. St. Canice's warned members not to transfer money in response to anyone claiming it needed to be moved to safety because of the breach. The CEO of Belfast-based Wellington IT, Colin Mitchell, said in a statement that the company notified the affected organizations "as soon as we confirmed the potential risk to customer data." He said Wellington IT has engaged outside cybersecurity experts to help investigate the breach, and reported the matter to the relevant authorities. Mitchell added: "We are directly supporting our customers in their assessment of the potential impact on affected individuals and to help them meet any applicable regulatory obligations. The capital's transport operator told The Register it first became aware something was amiss on November 16, when Oyster photocard customers started receiving emails asking them to create accounts they already had. The emails came from TfL's own systems, the transport body confirmed, but were generated as a result of the compromise. "We immediately took the TfL photocard website down while this was being investigated," said Shashi Verma, TfL's director of technology strategy and revenue. "The protection of personal information is a priority for us, and I apologize to our customers affected by this incident." TfL reckons its speedy response spared a considerable number of customers from having their details compromised. The transport operator says it has since contained the incident and contacted those potentially affected, though it is rather more forthcoming about what the hackers didn't get their hands on than what they did. TfL says no passwords, bank or payment card details, or customer journey information were compromised. It also believes the names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were unaffected. Among those whose accounts may have been compromised are holders of Zip Oyster cards – issued to children as young as five – as well as students, apprentices, care leavers, veterans, and Londoners aged 60 and over. Despite the assurances about passwords, TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change theirs, along with their security questions and answers. Those in the habit of recycling passwords across multiple websites are being advised to change them elsewhere, too. TfL says it has yet to find any evidence that the compromised data has been used and has notified the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO). The transport operator hasn't disclosed how the perpetrators got into its systems. Existing photocards will still let holders through the ticket barriers, though anyone needing to renew one or check their journey history will have to contact TfL's customer services team while the website is out of action . technology.title: Sticky note on monitor provided keys to the company’s kingdom
technology.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we talk smack about organizations that have smacked themselves down by practicing poor security hygiene. This week's story involves everyone's favorite low-tech password manager: the sticky note. Our terrifying tale comes courtesy of Christian Espinosa, a certified penetration tester with over 30 years of experience and the CEO of Blue Goat Cyber , a security company. Espinosa shared an experience where critical credentials were right out in the open for any person in the office to see. During a walkthrough of a client's office, he noticed a password written on a sticky note that was taped to an employee's monitor. While writing down your password and placing it in a physically secure paper notebook might be ok, taping it to the computer is definitely not. "Before I get my fingers on any system, I first walk the physical area that the system is located in — attackers do that when they're looking at a target too," Espinosa explained. “Physical security vulnerabilities are neglected much more often than technical security vulnerabilities and firms invest in firewalls where a sticky note is placed 3 feet from the front door." Espinosa took a photo of the sticky note and immediately tried logging into that employee's account. Success. Then, he tried the very same password on the VPN, which apparently had been maintained by that employee. Once he connected to the VPN, Espinosa had full access to the company network and all of its shared drives. Another document had instructions for how to log into the accounting server specifically. The accounting server was a particular treasure trove of client information. On that server, Espinosa found a folder with vendor banking information, invoices, and payment records. "At that point, a password I had read from a sticky note during a walk-through had taken me from one desk to information that could have been used for payroll fraud, identity theft, or vendor-payment fraud," Espinosa said. technology.title: Uncensored AI models are thriving on code hosting platforms
technology.description: Uncensored large language models (ULLMs) capable of producing harmful content are readily available at popular model-hosting websites, calling into question AI industry commitments to safety. Researchers affiliated with University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in the US and Nanyang Technological University in Singapore have analysed 22,096 ULLMs collected from five major LLM hosting platforms. As described in their paper , "Characterizing the Ecosystem of Open-Source Uncensored Large Language Models: Supply Chain, Governance, and Risks," authors Zilong Lin, Zichuan Li, Xiaojing Liao, and XiaoFeng Wang found that uncensored LLMs are easy to obtain from hosting platforms like US-based Hugging Face, Kaggle, and John Snow Labs, and China-based OpenCSG and ModelScope. What's more, these unrestrained models have been deployed through applications, GitHub projects, and model routing platforms like Open Router, and users of those apps or services may not be aware of the nature of the underlying LLM. "Uncensored LLMs generally refer to LLMs whose content filtering or refusal safeguards are absent, removed, or weakened, allowing them to respond to requests that aligned models may refuse," the paper explains. Zilong Lin, lead author and assistant professor of computer science at the University of Missouri-Kansas City, told The Register that open source LLM hosting platforms like Hugging Face play a similar role to code hosting services like GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg in the open source community by enabling sharing, modification, and redistribution of code artifacts. "However, unlike traditional software, whose behavior can often be examined through source code analysis, the safety alignment of LLMs is difficult to assess directly from their model files," Lin explained. "Evaluating whether an LLM has adequate safety safeguards typically requires deploying the model and testing its responses to potentially harmful prompts, which involves substantial computational and financial costs." Lin said this makes the identification and assessment of LLM safety particularly challenging, particularly given the large number of models available. That's why he and his colleagues chose to study the space through publicly available model metadata. Even popular commercial LLMs that are purportedly "aligned" – to some standard not everyone accepts – may respond to prompts with content deemed harmful. technology.title: Google continues model chemistry experiment with Neon
technology.description: Google periodically tables new AI models named after elements, and its latest offering has the noble name "Neon." "Engineered for long-running agent workflows, Neon sustains performance through complex, tool-heavy tasks end-to-end — whether running standalone or acting as a fast, high-judgment Orchestrator directing parallel Hydrogen subagents in Google Antigravity," explained Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, in a blog post . Neon emerged after Google last week emitted Hydrogen , after delivering Carbon two weeks earlier and wafting Argon out the door in late September. Unlike OpenAI's celestial more intuitive model naming scheme – Astra, Sol, Luna, and Terra – which maps celestial position to capability, Google's chemical soup doesn't suggest a specific hierarchy. To judge by price , Carbon or Argon would be Google's top tier model, based on non-discounted price that takes effect next month, each priced at $4/M input tokens, $20/M output. The Chocolate Factory refers to Carbon as "Our most capable reasoning model" while Argon is "Our efficient Gemini 4 frontier reasoning model … with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon across complex coding, agentic, math, and science tasks." Yet Neon, the latest element in the mix, surpasses both in Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index , scoring 61 compared to Carbon at 60, Hydrogen at 54, and Argon at 50. At the same time, Neon costs less, at $3/M input tokens and $15/M output. That favorable pricing is all the more surprising in light of Google's willingness, as of two days ago , to let users of its Gemini services opt out of generative AI model training without losing their chat histories. Kavukcuoglu evidently recognizes the need to clarify its model rankings, an issue addressed in a blog post section titled "Where Neon sits in the Gemini 4 family." "While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency," he explains. "Neon delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently." That may not really clarify which model is appropriate for which task and frankly Google is fine with that. As noted, Google Antigravity comes with an Orchestrator that decides how to spend your money for you by swapping models on the fly. As the company describes it, a developer might start a task using Carbon, which would write a plan, and hand the task off to Hydrogen to benefit from its token thrift. Antigravity does support model pinning , for those who know what they want. But Google, like other companies exploring model routing and orchestration, is fine with developers delegating decisions that affect billing to their trustworthy service provider. ®

technology.title: GTA VI didn’t break the internet, thanks to ‘stupid DNS tricks’
technology.description: Grand Theft Auto VI may put a dent in global productivity today but the game didn’t break the internet. For those unfamiliar, GTA VI is the first new instalment of the mega-hit game in 13 years and it is nearly impossible to understate the excitement surrounding its release. Anecdotal evidence suggests fans of the game may today report they suddenly feel unfit to perform paid work. Developer Rockstar Games allowed Xbox and PlayStation owners to pay for and download the 200GB-plus game on November 10, before play commenced on the 19 th . Millions took advantage of the chance to download the game, creating just the sort of internet traffic event that regional internet registry the Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre (RIPE NCC) can observe with its RIPE Atlas internet measurement network. RIPE data scientist Emile Aben, with help from staffers Alun Davies and James Cowie, went looking for GTA-related traffic and found some interesting patterns . Aben observed that traffic to PlayStations mostly came from content delivery networks operated by AWS and Fastly. Microsoft relied on Fastly for over half of traffic flowing to Xboxes and used Akamai too, but eschewed AWS's CloudFront. The data scientist observed heavy use of “GeoDNS,” a technique that returns different IP addresses for a single domain request, depending on a user’s location. DNS’s designers didn’t intend that. Indeed, the RIPE trio point out that Paul Vixie, the computer scientist who earned his place in the Internet Hall of Fame for massive contributions to the DNS system, regarded things like GeoDNS as “stupid DNS tricks.” Whatever you think of GeoDNS, the RIPE researchers found that folks who were likely downloading GTA VI from Los Angeles, Tokyo, and Istanbul were each directed to different sites. Their probe of a network in Shanghai, China, found “a very distinct long lookup-chain with a hostname that is associated with the Alibaba Cloud in the end that maps to six different IP addresses.” “This hints at specialised treatment for some countries/regions,” Aben wrote. He also noted that Internet Exchange Points, the interconnect facilities that network operators use to exchange traffic and shorten paths, had to cope with record traffic during the download period – and seem to have handled the load. Aben thinks the GTA VI download program offers a useful lesson. “DNS helps steer each player towards a download server, while multiple CDNs share the work of delivering the files,” he wrote. “That distribution matters beyond gaming. On the open Internet, game downloads share routers and link capacity with all kinds of other traffic, including critical services.” “Keeping downloads local helps leave capacity on long-distance links free for other uses, making that enormous demand manageable.” ®

technology.title: South Korea tries to out exam cheats with Extreme Emergency smartphone alert
technology.description: At 08:30 on Thursday morning every powered-on mobile phone in South Korea blared out an Extreme Emergency Alert tone for 10.5 seconds – but the nation was at peace, with no major natural disasters occurring. The extreme emergency South Korea hoped to avoid was cheating in the annual College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), an exam that over half a million people sit in the hope of securing admission to their preferred university. This year, around a third of those applicants are repeating the test after their previous effort didn’t get them the result they wanted. CSAT involves five separate examinations staged in a single day. Participants can only bring pencils to the test. Smartphones or any sort of tech is strictly forbidden. Which is why Korean authorities used the national alert system on the day of CSAT, because if the 40dB tone sounded in an exam centre, it could indicate a student had deliberately or inadvertently tried to bring a smartphone – perhaps as an exam aide. Korean media report the 08:30 alert turned up nine phones. Authorities will send a second alert tone at an unspecified time later in the day to again smoke out any surreptitious smartphones. It’s not possible to opt out of the alerts, one reason a concerned netizen has used the Android issue tracker to suggest sending alerts to detect exam cheats could be an abuse of the emergency alert system that Google might want to do something about. South Korea sends a lot of emergency alerts, for matters such as helping to find missing persons or to warn of dangerous weather. It’s not uncommon to receive several in a single day. Authorities also gave advance notice of the CSAT alerts, which will not, therefore, cause panic on the streets of Seoul or Busan. CSAT day is, however, a serious occasion. Some businesses open late so test-takers can get to their exams without having to battle peak hour traffic. Those measures are arguably less disruptive than the widespread internet outages that some states in India impose on major exam days. An alleged leak of one Indian exam paper saw the nation’s tech regulator ban messaging service Telegram in the country and eventually sparked a youth protest movement that New Delhi tried to suppress with more deliberate internet outages. ®

science.title: What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth?
science.description: null Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2 , launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s. Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035. So what's next for the two Voyager spacecraft as they reach further into interstellar space? Exploring afar Interstellar space, which is the area where the sun's constant stream of solar particles within the heliopause gives way to the physics of interstellar space, has been a valuable harvest for both Voyagers. Voyager 1 crossed interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to get data, while Voyager 2 has done the same since November 2018. "Current science is continuing our investigation on magnetic field strength and direction, plasma density, and energetic particle detection. What is important is to measure how these phenomena change as the spacecraft travels further away from the sun," Suzanne Dodd, project manager for the Voyager missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), told Space.com in an email. Added to that will be the Voyagers' examinations of plasma and magnetic fields nearby the spacecraft, and a focus on any "solar effects" such as shocks or pressure fronts, added JPL project scientist Linda Spilker in an email. "Key Voyager science going forward includes observing the extent to which our sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1," Spilker continued. "Where does the sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may last long enough to answer that question." The team also wants to watch the magnetic field around the spacecraft continue to change direction from the sun, to interstellar space, Spilker noted. That finding was not expected when the Voyagers launched, so scientists are curious to know more — as long as the spacecraft can last, that is. science.title: How aquanauts could help save Florida’s reefs
science.description: It sounds idyllic. Who wouldn’t want to occupy a newly built residence in the Florida Keys, complete with its own coral garden right outside the window? The only complication is that it is 17 metres below the surface of the Atlantic Ocean. That is not putting off Jim Brittsan, though. “This is really exciting,” he says. Brittsan is the founder and executive director of coral restoration non-profit Sustainable Ocean and Reefs (SOAR). He is also the diver who arranged the temporary coral nursery beside the residence, having brought the corals from a site where, 10 metres closer to the surface, they faced increasing environmental stress. Now, in reduced temperatures, they are starting to flourish, hosting their own marine life – visible day and night, in all its busyness, from the underwater residence known as Vanguard just 15 metres away. Vanguard was deployed at Tennessee Reef in June 2026 DEEP and Brendan Hall Vanguard is a long-stay underwater station for marine biologists. It was deployed in June 2026 at Tennessee Reef on the seafloor of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, around 8 kilometres south of Long Key. Its coral nursery looks like a strange marine shrubbery: the coral fragments are arranged on anchored ropes that stand upright in the water. Once Vanguard is operational, a more permanent nursery will be established and the corals will eventually be planted on the seabed as part of ongoing restoration efforts, with their long-term survival assessed through monitoring. Advertisement Resident scientists will be able to monitor marine life around the clock DEEP, the international design and engineering organisation that built Vanguard, aims to make humans aquatic by establishing more subsea habitats like it. These will allow people to live underwater for extended periods to engage in scientific research and conservation. This opens up unprecedented opportunities to do research because there is no need for divers to bounce up and down to a research vessel on the surface. Those round trips eat into valuable work hours, because divers can spend only limited time at depth and must ascend slowly to avoid decompression sickness. “If we’re diving from a boat, we can do about 3 hours’ work a day at depth,” Brittsan says. “It’s much more efficient if we can just stay down there.” Corals moved to deeper, cooler water beside Vanguard are recovering in a temporary nursery DEEP There is plenty of work to do in the Florida Keys. Elkhorn (Acropora palmata) and staghorn (Acropora cervicornis) corals, which are vital reef-building species, are now considered functionally extinct in Florida. But it is not just in Florida waters that corals are struggling. Climate change, which brings elevated ocean temperatures, is a significant threat to corals around the world. science.description: Turmeric capsules are touted as remedies for joint problems olga Yastremska/Alamy Turmeric supplements seem to have little to no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. That’s according to one of the most rigorous assessments of the evidence yet, which focused on four randomised controlled trials comparing the supplements to placebo pills. Osteoarthritis, which affects more than 500 million people worldwide , is caused by damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, resulting in pain, stiffness and inflammation. Standard treatments include painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs that can ease symptoms. “But many people see little or no benefit,” says Philip Conaghan at the University of Leeds, UK, who wasn’t involved in the latest review. Read more There are only a few anti-ageing supplements that actually work Turmeric supplements are often touted as an alternative therapy. They contain curcumin, a compound that gives turmeric its yellow colour and is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties. Yet such beliefs are often based on prior flawed studies , says Ivan Shirinsky at the Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine in Novosibirsk, Russia. Advertisement Shirinsky and his colleagues analysed results from four randomised controlled trials, collectively involving more than 370 participants with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomly assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills two or three times per day, for between eight weeks and three months. Each trial used a slightly different supplement containing a different curcumin dose. “We looked at the most rigorous evidence available,” says Shirinsky. Among those who took a placebo, knee pain decreased by 1.6 points, on average, on a scale from 0 to 10 by the end of the study. Those taking turmeric supplements experienced an average 2.3-point decrease in pain, meaning the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half that required to be meaningful to patients based on prior studies , says Shirinsky. science.description: null Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. (Image credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI); Acknowledgment: DSS, Robert Gendler) In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy . The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
science.description: null On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface , and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place. An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Mars MAVEN orbiter into space from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Base on Nov. 18, 2013. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) Why it mattered NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind , as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time. After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014 . The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind. An artist's view of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft at Mars on a mission to study its upper atmosphere. (Image credit: NASA) "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come." MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study. NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent , with NASA losing communication with the orbiter. science.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
science.description: null More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged. In the Grand Canyon, rock layers separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, revealing a vast gap in Earth's geological record. (Image credit: Marcia Straub via Getty Images) One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity. It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years. "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement . "The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance." The Great Unconformity imaged here shows 550 million year old Tapeats Sandstone resting on 1.7 billion year old Vishnu Schist, in Blacktail Canyon along the Colorado River in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. (Image credit: William Dummitt via Getty Images) What erased the geological record? However, when a short holiday break turns into a full holiday season, we know that this is a different “ball game”. Everyone has stress about something – some people love the holidays, and some people are holiday-avoidant… and some live in the middle. What specific stressors or challenges you experience might not bother your sibling, your spouse or your coworker. We want to be aware of and have a clear understanding of what holidays mean to you as a person. science.title: NASA Announces Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge for US Companies
science.description: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The Hall thruster is part of an Solar Electric Propulsion (SEP) system that uses 10 times less propellant than equivalent chemical rockets. Image Credit: NASA/Michelle M. Murphy (Wyle Information Systems, LLC) NASA launched a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration. Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical technology. NASA’s Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge is offering $500,000, split between two winning U.S. companies, to accelerate the maturation of mid-power systems that could be foundational to supporting future NASA and commercial missions. Interested parties can learn more at an AMPERE Virtual Industry Day hosted by NASA on Thursday, Nov. 19. “This challenge approach seeks to remove key barriers and facilitate commercialization by providing access to NASA subject matter expertise, state-of-the-art technologies, and world-class facilities at no cost to challenge winners,” said Dr. Jason Frieman, AMPERE project co-owner at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland. “We hope participants will see this as an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities to NASA and other government and commercial stakeholders.” The competition is the first of NASA’s Tech Maturation Prize series, which seeks to accelerate development of breakthrough technologies in support of NASA missions while strengthening the U.S. space economy. The competition includes three phases. In Phase 1, each participating team will submit a concept design, manufacturing plan, and cost and performance projections. NASA may select two winners to advance to Phase 2, where teams will develop prototypes and collaborate with NASA personnel. Through no-cost licensing, these teams can gain early access to NASA-developed Hall effect thruster technologies that use krypton as a propellant. In Phase 3, prototypes will be tested at NASA Glenn at no cost to the participating teams. In total, two winning teams may be selected to receive up to $250,000 each. The AMPERE Challenge is open for registration until Jan. 27, 2027, at 5 p.m. EST. science.title: New Scientist is 70 years old – join us in celebrating
science.description: Julianna Funk/Alamy Break open the bubbly, light the candles and get ready to party – New Scientist is 70 years old! Times have certainly changed since we published our first issue in 1956. Back then, some scientists had proposed that our carbon dioxide emissions were warming the planet, but the idea was controversial. Biologists were only beginning to unpick how DNA, whose structure had just been elucidated by Francis Crick, James Watson, Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, encoded the instructions for building organisms. The founders of this magazine couldn’t have envisaged the many ways that the web and smartphones would change daily life. We are even old enough that what once seemed futuristic is now pleasantly quaint. Launching our first website, Planet Science , in 1995, we declared that, “As the technologies mature, quite soon and at a terminal near you, it may be possible to hear interviews with well-known scientists”. Our digital offering has expanded greatly since then, with these sorts of interviews now available across our podcast and video channels. That said, we also speculated that it might be possible to “manipulate three-dimensional models of molecules” on a future version of our website, which we still haven’t quite managed to deliver. To mark our anniversary, we have put together a timeline of the biggest breakthroughs of the past 70 years . I enjoyed diving into our archives in search of how we reported era-defining moments. Our assessments haven’t always been on the money: after Yuri Gagarin’s space flight in 1961, for example, our correspondent declared “it is almost physically impossible for [the US] to beat the Russians to the moon”. But looking ahead is in New Scientist ‘s DNA, so, bravely – or foolishly – we press on.
